_comment: THE NAME RULES, as data. Generated into Go and Rust by cmd/gen-names.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Apps are Go, the badge host is Rust, and no library spans
them — so the rules were written twice, and VECTORS.tsv existed to DETECT the
drift between them. This file removes the drift instead: both implementations
are generated from here, so they cannot disagree about a character class or a
reserved name. The vectors stay, because they check something different — that
the generated code means what the rules intended.
WHAT IS NOT GENERATED: the prose. Every rule below has a reason, and the
reasons live in the hand-written names.go / names.rs beside the API. A
generator that emitted the explanations too would flatten exactly the part
EDIT HERE, then `make gen-names`. `make verify-names` fails if the checked-in

portable_chars._why: Lowercase only: FAT and Windows are case-insensitive, POSIX is not.

short_name_chars._why: What a FAT 8.3 field may hold. Anything else is replaced with '_'.

bad_edge._why: Windows silently strips some of these; a leading dot has no 8.3 form.
